entities.summary: Blackfriars Theatre was the name given to two separate theatres located in the former Blackfriars Dominican priory in the City of London during the Renaissance. The first theatre began as a venue for the Children of the Chapel Royal, child actors associated with the Queen's chapel choirs, and who from 1576 to 1584 staged plays in the vast hall of the former monastery. The second theatre dates from the purchase of the upper part of the priory and another building by James Burbage in 1596, which included the Parliament Chamber on the upper floor that was converted into the playhouse. Blackfriars Theatre is a theatre building in Europe. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Blackfriars Theatre played a significant role in the development of English theatre during the Renaissance, hosting performances by the Children of the Chapel Royal and later becoming a prominent venue for James Burbage's playhouse. Its influence can be seen in the evolution of English drama.
